history.title: Four chapters along one mountain ridge
history.description: A source-reviewed village narrative, from regional gazetteers and a physical road marker to today's Four Realms plan.

tang.title: Tang-era Lewen County: a regional horizon
tang.body: The Changshou District Gazetteer records the establishment of Lewen County in the Tang era, providing a time marker for the wider region. It is presented here as regional context, without equating an ancient county boundary or seat with present-day Zouma Village.
tang.source: Basis: administrative-history entries in the Changshou District Gazetteer; reviewed as regional history.

lychee.title: The lychee road: clues from Feiziyuan
lychee.body: The Fuzhou Gazetteer preserves a Tianbao-era reference to Feiziyuan, offering evidence of the historical relationship between lychee cultivation and mountain travel in the Changshou area. The Zouma ridge story connects orchard, road and seasonal journeys without inventing an exact route.
lychee.source: Basis: the Tianbao-era Feiziyuan entry in the Fuzhou Gazetteer; documentary clues are not presented as a proven route.

milestone.title: 1897: a stone guidepost
milestone.body: A guidepost dated to the twenty-third year of the Guangxu reign and unearthed on Zouma ridge is tangible evidence of historic movement. It brings the broad chronology of gazetteers down to the everyday scale of villagers and travelers finding their way.
milestone.source: Basis: the Guangxu 23 guidepost unearthed on Zouma ridge; future interpretation follows verified artifact records.

modern.title: Zouma today: Four Realms growing together
modern.body: Zouma Village in Fengcheng Subdistrict, Changshou District now organizes its rural experience through the Ancient Road, Lychee Field, Resilience Valley and Ridge Dwelling realms. This village is not Zouma Ancient Town in Jiulongpo District; they are separate places.
modern.source: Basis: the contemporary Four Realms plan; location verified as Zouma Village, Fengcheng Subdistrict, Changshou District, Chongqing.

adopt.title: Select the annual plan and enter pending payment
adopt.body: Choose LZ-018 and the annual plan from the adoption list. The system creates a pending-payment demo state; WeChat and Alipay charging are not connected.

accept.title: Villager accepts the care task
accept.body: After OTP login, the villager reviews the deadline, demo task amount, and care photo requirements. Rejection or timeout enters operations exception handling.

evidence.title: Upload care photos and notes
evidence.body: This task needs at least two photos that clearly show the tree and the care result. Missing photos or upload failures explain how to submit again.

review.title: Operations rejects once, then approves
review.body: The demo keeps two care-record versions: an unclear photo is returned, the villager adds material, and a reviewer confirms the result. The reviewer must explain what is missing.

benefit.title: Check adoption benefits, settlement and renewal
benefit.body: After care-record approval, review harvest delivery benefits, task settlement and renewal. Refund requests only create a human-review ticket.

badCase.title: Explain rule limits with one Bad Case
badCase.body: Finish with an event chain for prolonged rain, task delay or delayed benefits, and explain why simulation cannot prove business value or automatically promote rules.

boundaries.title: What this demo will not decide for you
boundaries.body: The project only tests flows, permissions and rules. The actions below are not live and are never decided directly by AI.
boundaries.payment: Real WeChat and Alipay charging is not connected; pending payment is a demo workflow state.
boundaries.refund: A refund request only creates a human-review ticket. Operations staff must confirm how the adoption and unclaimed benefits are handled.
boundaries.agent: AI only organizes notes, checks material completeness and drafts review comments. It cannot modify orders or settlements.
boundaries.review: Operations staff confirm care-record reviews, exception responsibility and settlement release.
